lore_anchors.definition: A catastrophic event where a massive number of demon beasts flood out of their natural habitat, overwhelming human settlements. In xianxia, it functions as a natural disaster and a plot device to reset the political map.

A severe cultivation injury caused by attempting to use a technique that exceeds the practitioner's current base, causing internal energy to spiral out of control. It is a mechanical failure, not a disease.
A spell or ritual placed on a subordinate's body by a master, allowing the master to inflict punishment or trigger death remotely. It is the cultivation world's equivalent of an unbreakable contract.
A key Confucian virtue in Chinese culture emphasizing devotion and duty to one's parents. In this context, it is the emotional justification for a desperate transaction.
A cultivator who has reached the Nascent Soul stage, a level of power that fundamentally changes their existence. They are the 'walking strategic weapons' of the lower realms.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Han Li so silent at the end of the chapter?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is running a silent cost-benefit analysis. The Mortal Stream doesn't reward impulsive kindness; it rewards calculated risk management. He is weighing the value of a willing servant against the risk of exposure and future obligation.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is this 'Institutional Tribulation' a new term?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes, it is a confirmed high-stakes conflict type in the Mortal Stream. It refers to a protagonist having to navigate crushing political hierarchies, wartime systems, and institutional pressure with the same cold calculation as a physical battle.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Did the Inner Star Seas really abandon the Outer Star Seas?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes, that is the explicit implication in the text. This reinforces the brutal Dark Forest logic of the cultivation world: if a territory is too expensive to hold and defend, the central powers will rationally choose to let it burn and seal off the border.
